status_reason: Experiment 1 as published: the double-drift stimulus (2 c/dva, sigma 0.1 dva, 3 dva path at 2 dva/s, 3 Hz drift reversing with the path, 10 dva right of fixation), the perceptual task with interleaved adaptive staircases and arrow-key reports, and the saccade task at the perceived-vertical orientations with a no-drift control, six fixation-offset times and gaze-contingent removal. Changes are substitutions of apparatus and software (QUEST+ placement, online saccade detection), listed as deviations; Experiment 2 is not included.

original.citation: Lisi, M., & Cavanagh, P. (2015). Dissociation between the perceptual and saccadic localization of moving objects. Current Biology, 25(19), 2535-2540.
original.experiments: Experiment 1: the perceptual task and the saccade task (Experiment 2, the mid-path gap, is not included)

notes: Software verification only (tests and simulated sessions with a simulated observer); no participant data have been recorded with this folder. The saccade task needs each participant's perceived-vertical orientations from the perceptual task: run that first and enter its PSEs (python -m lisi_cavanagh2015.pse).
